Professional Summary

Senior SAP EWM ABAP Consultant with 13+ years of hands-on SAP development experience since 2013 and a dedicated focus on SAP S/4HANA Extended Warehouse Management since 2022. SAP Certified in both ABAP (Development Associate) and EWM with SAP S/4HANA (Application Associate). Co-Founder of DebuggerTR Consulting, delivering EWM projects through partnerships with Capgemini and, previously, Westernacher, with a portfolio of 30+ enterprises including Asahi Beverages, Infineon, Boston Scientific, Wärtsilä, Essity, Siemens, Swarovski, Unilever and Mercedes-Benz.

Core strength is end-to-end EWM development: MFS and warehouse automation integration, RF Framework, Warehouse Monitor, PPF/output and Adobe Forms, plus integration with TM, MES and external systems via IDoc, RFC/BAPI and OData. Works exclusively in Object-Oriented ABAP with ABAP Unit and test doubles, applies SAP HANA code pushdown through CDS Views and AMDP, and delivers ATC-clean, Clean Core-compliant code with zero open Priority 1/2 findings at transport release, including in GxP-validated landscapes. MUSTAFA YILMAZ – PROJECT PORTFOLIO

Detailed project overview with SAP module coverage, code quality governance and Clean Core compliance. Westernacher project dates may overlap because assignments were delivered under one full-time consultancy engagement with dynamic parallel allocation. Since November 2026, DebuggerTR projects are delivered through a partnership with Capgemini. Labels such as WFI, FP and WHM are customer/project naming abbreviations, not SAP technology names.

[P01] Asahi Beverages

EWM ABAP Developer

@ DebuggerTR Consulting (via Capgemini)

November 2026 – Present | Remote · Melbourne, Australia

Modules: S/4HANA EWM · MFS · RF · ABAP OO · CDS

Matrix project — SAP S/4HANA EWM implementation for Asahi Beverages, delivered as a Capgemini project. EWM ABAP development covering Material Flow System (MFS) integration with warehouse automation (PLC communication, telegram processing, communication points and conveyor/automated-storage control logic), RF enhancements, process-specific BAdIs and custom ABAP for beverage warehouse and distribution processes. Delivered fully remotely from Riga for the Melbourne-based project team, bridging a 9–10 hour time-zone difference through planned overlap hours, structured asynchronous handovers and reliable delivery against Australian business-day deadlines.

Code Quality & Clean Core: Development follows SAP’s Clean Core extensibility model — enhancements implemented only through released BAdIs, released APIs and released CDS views, with no modifications to SAP standard objects, so the EWM and MFS layer stays upgrade-stable. Every object is released only after a clean ABAP Test Cockpit (ATC) run against the project check variant, including Clean Core / cloud-readiness, performance and security checks; zero open Priority 1 and Priority 2 findings at transport release, plus mandatory peer code review. MFS telegram handling and custom warehouse logic are built in Object-Oriented ABAP with ABAP Unit test classes and test doubles, so automation scenarios can be regression-tested without a live PLC connection. Clean ABAP applied throughout — single-responsibility classes, descriptive naming, class-based exceptions and SAP HANA code pushdown via CDS Views for data-intensive selections.

[P02] Infineon

EWM ABAP Developer

@ DebuggerTR Consulting (via Westernacher)

October 2025 – July 2026 | Remote

Modules: TM · S/4HANA EWM · RF · Warehouse Monitor

Decentralised SAP S/4HANA EWM. TM_EWM Template & Wave 1 implementation covering TM/EWM template development, RF screens, Warehouse Monitor enhancements, process-specific BAdIs, forms/output and integration work.

Code Quality & Clean Core: All template objects released only after a clean ABAP Test Cockpit (ATC) run against the customer’s global check variant; zero open Priority 1 and Priority 2 findings at transport release. Built entirely in Object-Oriented ABAP with ABAP Unit test classes covering the reusable template logic, so that each subsequent wave inherits an executable regression suite. Applied Clean ABAP principles throughout — single-responsibility methods, descriptive naming without cryptic abbreviations, and class-based exception handling instead of legacy SY-SUBRC chains, in line with SAP Clean Core extensibility guidance.

[P03] RS Group

EWM ABAP Developer

@ DebuggerTR Consulting (via Westernacher)

September 2025 – October 2025 | Remote

Modules: S/4HANA EWM · ABAP OO

Decentralised SAP S/4HANA EWM. EWM development project for RS Group’s distribution operations. Custom warehouse process development, enhancements, and S/4HANA EWM integration.

Code Quality & Clean Core: Executed ATC checks with the S4HANA_READINESS and performance check variants on every transport; remediated all findings related to obsolete statements, SELECT * usage and missing index access before release. Refactored legacy procedural routines into Object-Oriented ABAP following Clean ABAP guidance — short methods, no global mutable state, and constants instead of magic numbers — with ABAP Unit tests written against the new classes to prove behaviour was preserved through the refactoring. Applied SAP HANA code pushdown by moving heavy selection logic into CDS Views and AMDP methods instead of ABAP-side loops. Enhancements implemented via released BAdIs to preserve upgrade stability under Clean Core.

[P04] Boston Scientific

EWM ABAP Developer

@ DebuggerTR Consulting (via Westernacher)

October 2024 – August 2025 | Remote

Modules: S/4HANA EWM · RF · Warehouse Monitor · D3/D3A · Forms/Output

Decentralised SAP S/4HANA EWM. EWM Magellan D3/D3A rollout for medical-device manufacturing and distribution. Hands-on RF development, Warehouse Monitor enhancements, process-specific BAdIs, forms/output and custom ABAP. For the automated packing area, developed SAP/EWM-side control logic to ensure the required product leaflet/prospectus was printed and its inclusion was confirmed as part of the packing flow before completion.

Code Quality & Clean Core: Operating in a validated (GxP-relevant) medical device landscape, every object passed a documented ATC review with evidence attached to the change record. Mandatory peer code review plus ATC sign-off before QA transport. ABAP Unit test classes written for reusable EWM logic and executed as repeatable evidence of correct behaviour — a decisive advantage in a validated environment where re-testing must be demonstrable. Clean ABAP applied with emphasis on readability and traceability: self-documenting method names, explicit typing, and dependency-injected classes isolated from the database so they can be tested with test doubles.

[P05] Wärtsilä

EWM ABAP Developer

@ DebuggerTR Consulting (via Westernacher)

November 2023 – August 2025 | Remote

Modules: S/4HANA EWM · MFS · AMS · CR/CI

Decentralised SAP S/4HANA EWM AMS / CR-CI assignment with a strong hands-on MFS focus. Developed the SAP EWM/MFS-side housekeeping solution that analysed next-day delivery demand, determined the stock required for morning operations, planned the necessary overnight warehouse movements and pre-positioned products into fast-pick bins. Also supported bug fixing, performance optimisation and enhancements around the live warehouse process.

Code Quality & Clean Core: Each CR/CI delivery gated by ATC checks; the AMS quality KPI required no new Priority 1/2 findings to be introduced by any change. Introduced ABAP Unit tests around recurring defect areas so that every fixed bug was locked in by a test — measurably reducing regression tickets in a support-driven engagement. Used ATC performance checks to drive the CI backlog, identifying nested SELECT statements and unbuffered table access, then refactoring them into set-based operations and CDS-based selections. Progressive Clean ABAP refactoring of touched code (boy-scout rule) reduced technical debt across the AMS scope.

[P10] Siemens

SAP Interface Development Lead

@ Walldorf Consulting AG

LDA (Logistics Data Automation) project at Siemens. During the 2022–2023 transition, I completed the remaining Siemens/LDA responsibilities part-time with Walldorf Consulting AG’s knowledge and approval while DebuggerTR Consulting was established, before moving fully to my own company.

Code Quality & Clean Core: As development lead, defined and enforced the team’s ATC check variant and made an ATC-clean result a precondition for merge and transport release. Reviewed team members’ findings and coached on remediation rather than exemption. Interface layer built in Object-Oriented ABAP to Clean ABAP standards — explicit interfaces, dependency injection, and structured error handling with full message logging. Introduced ABAP Unit tests with mocked RFC/IDoc endpoints so interface mappings could be verified without a connected partner system, which removed a major dependency from the test cycle.

[P11] Arvato Systems – Multiple Projects

SAP Technical Lead / ABAP Quality Team Lead

@ Arvato Systems Latvia

January 2019 – June 2022 | Riga, Latvia

Modules: S/4HANA · IS-U · ABAP OO · ZUGFeRD · Adobe Forms · SolMan ChaRM

Led QA and ABAP Development teams across multiple parallel projects: S/4HANA conversion, SIMS, Lekarland, ZUGFeRD (e-Invoicing to the German standard), IS-U (Industry Solution Utilities), and the Apollo project. Responsible for technical architecture, code reviews, team mentoring, and end-to-end quality governance across a dual-landscape environment.

Code Quality & Clean Core: Owned the central ATC governance model for the ABAP team — defined the global check variant, enabled ATC blocking mode in the development systems for Priority 1 and Priority 2 findings at transport task and request level, and acted as approver in the ATC exemption workflow. Exemptions required written justification and an expiry date and could not be self-approved by the requesting developer. Established Clean ABAP and Object-Oriented ABAP as the team-wide written standard, made ABAP Unit test coverage a review criterion for new development, and used CDS Views and AMDP for HANA-side processing during the S/4HANA conversion.

SolMan ChaRM, Retrofit & ABAP Quality Team Leadership:

  • SAP Solution Manager (ChaRM): managed the full change control lifecycle — Requests for Change, Change Documents, and transport task/release handling through the ChaRM status schema, ensuring no transport bypassed the approved change path.
  • Dual-landscape retrofit: operated a parallel maintenance and project (implementation) landscape and ran the retrofit process so maintenance changes were consistently carried into the S/4HANA project track without regression.
  • Cross-System Object Lock (CSOL): used CSOL to detect and manage conflicting object changes across the two landscapes early, resolving collisions before they reached QA.
  • Retrofit conflict resolution: handled automatic, semi-automatic (SAP Correction Workbench / BC-Set) and fully manual retrofit cases, with manual code merges for objects that could not be transferred automatically.
  • ATC quality gate ownership: configured and maintained the check variants, scheduled periodic full-package ATC runs, and tracked finding trends as a team quality KPI rather than a one-off check.
  • Code review process: ran structured peer reviews on every transport — reviewing ATC results, Clean ABAP conformance, performance-critical database access, security-relevant authority checks, and adherence to the agreed architecture.
  • Exemption governance: assessed exemption requests as lead reviewer — approving, rejecting, or returning to the applicant for further justification, keeping the exemption backlog auditable.
  • Custom code readiness for S/4HANA: applied the Simplification Database via the S4HANA_READINESS check variant to identify and remediate incompatible custom code ahead of the conversion.
  • ABAP Unit adoption: introduced unit testing as a team standard — defined where test classes were mandatory, reviewed test quality alongside production code, and used test doubles to decouple tests from the database.
  • Team enablement: onboarded and mentored ABAP developers on Object-Oriented ABAP, Clean ABAP, ABAP Unit, ATC usage, and the ChaRM/retrofit workflow, raising first-pass review success rates across the team.
